questions.prompt: In what units is energy measured?
What units is force measured in?

Look at this picture.  This is an example of:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch155","id":"e389-image1"}]}]
questions.explanation: The picture intends Newton’s third law:interaction forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies. The diagram is simplified;identify the two interacting bodies rather than claiming the pair cancels on one body.

questions.prompt: A ball is sitting still on the ground.  It will not move until someone kicks it.  This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The intended example is inertia/Newton’s first law;zero resultant force leaves the ball at rest in the chosen inertial frame.

questions.prompt: A Cricket player hits a ball with a bat. The action force is the impact of the bat against the ball. The reaction force is…
options: The grip of the player’s hands on the ball
The air resistance on the ball
The force of the ball against the bat.
questions.explanation: The ball exerts the opposite interaction force on the bat. Action and reaction are simultaneous forces on different bodies.

questions.prompt: A force can be described as:
options: How fast an object is moving.
A push or a pull on an object.
questions.explanation: A push or pull is the intended introductory force description.

questions.prompt: Which  of the following shows velocity?
options: a bus takes John to school.

questions.prompt: A 90 N force is applied to a 65 kg mass. The mass will accelerate at:
A spaceship is moving through space at 25,000 km/h.  It will not change speed or direction unless something acts on it.  This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Newton’s first law:constant velocity without a nonzero resultant external force.
